target_customer: Data teams at companies running a cloud data warehouse stack, such as Klaviyo, Ramp and Bose
problem: Data teams learn about broken or wrong data from executives or customers. Metaplane monitors warehouse tables and lineage to catch silent data quality issues early.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription priced by monitored tables or usage tier

founders.name: Kevin Hu
founders.background_notes: Did machine learning and data visualization research at MIT per a press profile.

founders.name: Peter Casinelli
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder in the Series A press release; not on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed warehouse connectors, anomaly detection on metadata and column level lineage. Standard engineering with some hard ML and SQL parsing work, doable by a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Many entrants offered similar monitoring, and the product depended on warehouse metadata access. Integrations and lineage added some switching cost.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Snowflake Ventures invested in 2024 and Datadog acquired Metaplane in April 2025, announced as a standalone Metaplane by Datadog offering.

market_need_then: The cloud data stack (warehouses and dbt) was spreading, and data teams lacked tooling to detect incidents; the data observability category was being defined around 2019.

branding.domain_note: Used metaplane.dev rather than a .com; no purchase story found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and benefit focused: Be the first to know about data incidents, set up in 15 minutes, no credit card required.

rebrands.why: Post acquisition endorsement while keeping the product standalone.

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive coined compound name with a clear developer voice, but no sourced evidence of mascot, merch or community, and no press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Metaplane rode the cloud data stack wave with a fast setup monitoring product, reached 100 plus customers by 2023, raised an 8.4 million dollar seed in January 2023 and a 13.8 million dollar Series A in March 2024, and was acquired by Datadog in April 2025 as Datadog expanded from software into data observability. The exit price was not disclosed and the category was crowded, so the sale looks like a strategic fit rather than a clear market win.
notes: Total raised 22.2 million dollars per the company equals seed plus Series A, but CB Insights counts 7 rounds and PitchBook says 23.8 million, so small earlier or later amounts (YC deal, Snowflake Ventures in 2024) may exist. Competitor list left empty: only 2026 vendor comparison pages were found, with no source dated near early 2020. Monte Carlo is credited by vendor blogs with coining data observability in 2019 but that was not verified from a dated source. Founding year varies by source (2019 most common).
